To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the first-pass gated format scintigraphic method with a variable ROI is reliable for determination of RVEF, 2) the beat-by-beet and equilibrium MUGA methods consistently under estimate RVEF, and 3) the scintigraphically determined RVEF values correlated best with the RVEF values obtained by cine CT.

the scintigraphically determined RVEF values using the first-pass gated format (variable ROI) were significantly higher and correlated significantly better with the RVEF values measured using the cine CT method than did the RVEF determined with the other two techniques.

the scintigraphically derived RV ejection fraction is underestimated by equilibrium MUGA and by beat-by-beat methods, but that the best correlation with CT was obtained with a first-pass MUGAs technique using variable ROI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a method for the non-invasive determination of cardiac output (CO) by means of the first-pass method.
a new method for the determination of the ejection fraction of the right ventricle by scintigraphic means.
the determination of the right ventricular ejections fraction (RVE) by means of scintigraphic techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scintigraphically derived RVEF is not a reliable indicator of RV function.
the use of the first-pass gated format is the preferred method for determination of the right ventricular ejections fraction.

the first-pass gated method is the most accurate method for the determination of right ventricle ejection fraction, but the beat by beat technique is the most accurate for the determination of left ventricle ejections fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first pass MUGA technique with a variable ROI is a reliable noninvasive method to determine RVEF.
a scintigraphic method of first-pass gated format and variable ROI is reliable by correlation with Cine CT as a noninvasive and inexpensive method for evaluation of right ventricular function.
the use of a variable ROI in a first-pass gated acquisition format is the best method currently available for determination and quantitation of RVEF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the first-pass MIGA technique is a reliable, inexpensive, and noninvasive method to evaluate RV function.
there is no need to use the first pass method for RV ejection fraction determination in patients with low RV ejection fractions (EFs), as this method will underestimate the RV EF.
there is a need for more accurate and reliable methods for determining RV volumes and ejection fraction.
